name: Document-VLM inference provider
one_line: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving an open VLM (Qwen2.5-VL-7B measured) at a published accuracy-per-dollar operating point for document pages, sold on a same-pages rerunnable benchmark; the technical lever is a resize config flag, the dollar side is modeled, and the in-engine moat is blocked.
evidence_grade_reason: The technical lever (visual-token budget vs accuracy frontier: 2.7x throughput at -1.0 pt from 1536px to 1024px) was measured once, in-engine (vLLM 0.24.0, A100-80GB), on 200 DocVQA pages, one run, relaxed match, offline eager batch — B-grade on its own. But the brief's core value claim is bounded and contradicted: the accuracy-parity half rests on a 200-page relaxed-match head-to-head against a 2024 model (GPT-4o) whose run output was never recorded beyond one number; the cost half has never been measured in dollars (the repo's headline '~40x cheaper' is a pricing model whose 56px-per-token formula contradicts the repo's own measured 1,017/2,201 prompt tokens, collapsing to ~9-10x at the same assumed rates); the moat (in-model pruning) is blocked with no result; and against a same-config vLLM baseline the engine advantage is 1.0x by construction.
build_cost_weeks_to_proof: 3-5 weeks to the first credible public proof (estimate): an ANLS benchmark on >= 1,000 DocVQA validation pages with bootstrap CIs, Qwen2.5-VL-7B and Qwen3-VL-8B on vLLM in serving mode with logged GPU-seconds, versus gpt-5.4 / gpt-5.6-luna / Gemini 3.8 Flash (medium) / Claude Haiku 4.5 / DeepSeek V4-flash-vision with usage-based $/1K pages, plus Textract Queries and Azure query fields as native OCR-QA baselines, published with the harness. Assumptions: 1-2 engineers; vendor accounts for Azure/GCP/AWS/DeepSeek obtained in week 1 (the main slip risk); Qwen3-VL-8B loads on vLLM 0.24.0 (unverified in-repo); roughly 15-25 A100-hours (estimate; at Modal's $2.50/hr about $40-65) plus a few hundred dollars of API spend (estimate). The moat spike is off this path. A sellable metered endpoint (auth, payments, batch queue, SSE, SLA) is 8-10 weeks (estimate), given the gaps in 03-build-inventory.md (no OAuth callback, no payments, Dockerfile omits control/, stream forced off).

factcheck.correction: Tensormesh does list reserved H200 at $2.50/hr, but the relevant anchor is Modal's A100-80GB rate of $2.50/hr (05-research-gpu-pricing.md), the platform the eval actually ran on; RunPod A100-80GB is $1.39-1.59. Re-anchored to $1.39-2.50/GPU-hour A100-80GB.

factcheck.claim: 'A deployable endpoint config exists at the measured operating point' (max_pixels 1,048,576)
factcheck.correction: max_pixels 1,048,576 is not the 1024-long-side point. Running pricing.py's smart-resize at 28 px/token, a full-resolution page of DocVQA-like aspect lands at ~896x1148 = 1,312 tokens, an unmeasured point between the 1024 row (1,017) and 1536 row (2,201); the endpoint reproduces the measured point only if the client pre-resizes to <= 1024 long side. Added to Proven caveats, Unproven table, and the build plan (enforce 1024 resize).

attacks.attack: The proof benchmark does not isolate a product advantage. The 2.7x is a resize any client applies before upload or any self-hoster sets with --mm-processor-kwargs max_pixels (evals/RESULTS.md's own caveat). Against vanilla vLLM or SGLang at the same max_pixels the pages/GPU-hour advantage is 1.0x by construction, so the draft's 'advantage vs vanilla-vLLM default' gate would pass trivially while proving nothing about the engine.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Run vanilla vLLM and SGLang with the same Qwen weights and the same max_pixels on the same A100 and pages; if pages/GPU-hour is within noise of the endpoint (expected), drop every engine-advantage claim and sell operating point + benchmark + billing, or pass the moat gate first. Revised brief adds this as Class 1 baseline and a founder decision.

attacks.attack: Serving cost is unmeasured and the measured throughput is the most favorable case: one offline llm.chat batch of 200 prompts, enforce_eager=True, 32-token outputs, no concurrency, no p95, no cold starts. The endpoint runs max_inputs=32 per container with scale-to-zero and a 900 s startup timeout. Realized $/page at real utilization could be several-fold above the $0.013-0.023/1K floor.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: vllm bench serve-style load at 8/32/128 concurrency in serving mode logging GPU-seconds per page, p50/p95 TTFT and cold-start share; publish $/1K at the observed utilization. Kill gate: > $0.42/1K at 50% utilization.

attacks.attack: The workload the value proposition assumes (32-token answers) is not the IDP workload the pricing pages describe (transcription and extraction, 1,500-3,000 output tokens per page per Claude's PDF docs). For long outputs the visual-token lever only shrinks prefill and attention context; per-token decode work at small batch is unchanged, so the 2.7x can collapse toward 1x. No measurement exists.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Rerun modal_vlm_frontier.py with a transcription prompt and max_tokens 1,500 at 768/1024/1536; kill if 1024 vs 1536 pages/GPU-hour < 1.3x, proceed at >= 2.0x.

attacks.attack: Sample size and scorer. 200 pages, one run: the -1.0 pt operating-point loss is 2 pages and the 4.5-pt GPT-4o gap is 9 pages; the scorer counts 'gold substring in prediction' as correct; ANLS (the metric every vendor table uses) was never computed; the GPT-4o run output beyond one number is unrecorded.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: ANLS with bootstrap CIs on N >= 1,000 DocVQA validation pages for both models; kill if Qwen minus GPT-4o < +1.0 pt ANLS.

attacks.attack: GPT-4o is a 2024 comparator. Vendor tables already put open 8B above GPT-5 on DocVQA (96.1 vs 91.5), and the cheap tiers that matter today are unmeasured: gpt-5.6-luna (~$0.25/1K page), Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite ($0.30/M), and DeepSeek V4-flash-vision (<= 384 tokens/image, ~$0.17/1K peak, ~$0.08 off-peak), which sits below the draft's hosted-Qwen anchor. If any of them matches within 1 pt at a comparable price, the price-led pitch has no room.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Week-2 run: those tiers on the same pages with usage-based $/1K; kill if any is within 1 pt ANLS at <= 2x the measured price.

attacks.attack: The moat is blocked and, even if unblocked, mis-specified. modal_vlm_moat.py (a) runs on the HF path with transformers 4.49.0, not vLLM, so a positive result still needs a vLLM model-code port; (b) measures accuracy only, while the pruned path still runs the ViT at 1280px, so its throughput at matched LLM tokens is below resize's; (c) defaults to n=80; and (d) vLLM RFC #45098 proposes --image-pruning-rate with Qwen3-VL as the example, so a merge turns the 'execution-owned' lever into an OSS flag.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Reimplement get_rope_index for the pruned set, run at n >= 200 with img/s per method; proceed only if best prune minus resize >= +0.02 AND prune img/s >= 0.8x resize; track the RFC.

attacks.attack: The deployed config is not the measured operating point. max_pixels 1,048,576 smart-resizes a full-resolution page to ~896x1148 = 1,312 tokens (arithmetic from pricing.py at 28 px/token), between the 1024 (1,017) and 1536 (2,201) rows, unmeasured; only a client pre-resize to 1024 long side reproduces 0.925 / 30.2 img/s.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Add 1148px to BUDGETS and measure, or enforce a 1024 long-side resize in the preprocessor (added to the plan).

attacks.attack: Version and API dependence. vLLM 0.24.0 is pinned; Qwen3-VL-8B support in that version is unverified in the repo; the moat path depends on transformers 4.49.0 internals. Unlike the stateful-session direction, this one does not depend on the experimental KVConnector API, which limits the exposure.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: A one-hour smoke run of Qwen3-VL-8B on vLLM 0.24.0 before Week 1 commits to it.

attacks.attack: The 6-week plan slips at Week 2 and Weeks 4-5. Week 2 needs accounts and adapters for nine vendors, and cloud OCR products mostly do not answer questions (Document AI has no QA endpoint; Textract Queries and Azure query fields do), so the draft's drop-in adapters become pipelines. Weeks 4-5 add a durable batch queue, PDF rasterizer, per-page meter, SSE and a Dockerfile fix on a control plane with no OAuth callback and no payments (03-build-inventory.md), so 'design partners onboarded in Week 5' has no billing path.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Not a measurement: the revised plan moves the public proof to Week 3, makes the moat spike optional, and states that payments/OAuth/SLA are outside six weeks (8-10 weeks estimate to a sellable endpoint).

attacks.attack: Workload assumptions are unsupported by the research files: no customer interviews, no page mix, no resolution distribution, no concurrency pattern; multi-page documents exceed the one-image / 8192-token config; the 'backlog-concentrated' shape is inferred from batch discounts.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: Five design partners share a workload sample (page mix, resolution, output type, concurrency, idle pattern) before pricing is set.

attacks.attack: Per-page pricing is not unique. Gemini bills a PDF page at a fixed 560 tokens at medium (effectively per page), and Mistral OCR, Reducto, LlamaParse, Extend, Unstructured and the cloud OCR APIs already bill per page; the draft's competitive table said frontier labs lack per-page pricing.
attacks.what_would_settle_it: None; stated neutrally in sections 8 and 9.

missing_founder_decisions: Whether the proof must include an engine advantage at all (the draft assumed 'advantage vs vanilla vLLM' was the decisive gate; against a same-config baseline it is 1.0x) or whether operating point + benchmark + billing suffices.
Per-page billing: section 8 of the draft decided 'Bill per page' while section 11 listed it as open; per page vs per token vs per-GPU-hour dedicated is now explicitly the founder's.
Hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint as the MVP shape: the draft's plan assumed hosted while listing hosted vs BYOC vs harness-only as a decision.
DocVQA ANLS as the proof metric: it is saturated (vendor tables put open 8B above GPT-5); olmOCR-Bench/OmniDocBench transcription or a design partner's extraction F1 are alternatives.
The accuracy bar: parity with GPT-4o (2024, the only measured comparator) vs with current cheap tiers (gpt-5.6-luna, Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, DeepSeek V4-flash-vision).
Moat sprint timing: the repo recorded 'gate the moat sprint on market validation'; the draft scheduled it in Week 6 regardless; before/after/never is the founder's.
GPU class and cloud: all measurements are A100-80GB on Modal at $2.50/hr; RunPod A100 $1.39-1.59, H100 $2.69-3.95, MI300X $2.59-2.99, MI355X $2.29-2.95 move the modeled floor by about 2x.
Whether DeepSeek V4-flash-vision at ~$0.08-0.17/1K images (accuracy unmeasured) is an adjacency that matters.
Product shape: QA/extraction (measured) vs full-page transcription (unmeasured economics) vs both; and which transcription model if so (olmOCR-2, dots.mocr, DeepSeek-OCR).
Concurrency target and SLA (Reducto sells 200/350/500+ concurrent pages; the endpoint is max_inputs=32 per container with scale-to-zero).
Data policy: zero-data-retention (Morph and Wafer offer it) vs retaining customer pages to build the benchmark corpus.
Whether to publish the compute floor and the batch/standby tier discount (the draft assumed a Morph/DeepSeek-style 50% tier).
strongest_version: The strongest honest form is a benchmark-led document-VLM service: publish, from one open harness, ANLS and measured dollars per thousand pages for an open 7-8B VLM at a fixed 1024px operating point against the frontier cheap tiers, DeepSeek's 384-token vision model, and the native OCR question-answering endpoints, on the same pages the same day, and let buyers rerun it on their own PDFs. What is already in hand is real but narrow: one in-engine measurement showing 0.925 relaxed-match accuracy at 30.2 pages/s on an A100 (2.7x the 1536px point for a 1.0-pt loss) and a 200-page head-to-head above GPT-4o. The service sells the operating point, per-page metering and the benchmark, stated openly as a configuration-and-billing product with no engine advantage over a same-config vLLM; if the design partners convert on that, the time-boxed in-model pruning sprint (blocked today by Qwen2.5-VL's mRoPE grid) is the one path to an execution-owned lever, and its gate is pre-registered with both an accuracy and a throughput bar. Everything that would make this a cost story rather than an accuracy story (serving-mode $/page at real utilization, transcription-length outputs, the cheap tiers on the same pages) is unmeasured and is the first three weeks of work.
